record.paper_title: On Global Hyperbolicity of Spacetimes: Topology Meets Functional Analysis
record.context_brief: Reconstructing spacetime topology from interval domains
record.original_question: Given the equivalence between the category of globally hyperbolic posets and the category of interval domains, can the topology of a spacetime be reconstructed in a technically rigorous way from the topology of an interval domain? Moreover, since topologies such as the Zeeman fine topology, Göbel’s generalization, and the Hawking–King–McCarthy topology are not metrizable, does that non-metrizability help identify an appropriate spacetime topology other than the manifold topology when interval domains are taken as the underlying order-theoretic model?

evidence.quote: Question 3: In the light of Theorem 3.8, we ask whether the topology of a spacetime can be reconstructed, in some technical and rigorous way, from the topology of an interval domain.

The spacetime topologies that we have mentioned in this section, like for example the Zeeman fine topology or its generalization by Göbel, or the one by Hawking-King-McCarthy are not metrizable; does this give us any insight on the appropriate candidate for a spacetime topology (other than the manifold topology), given that interval domains are order-theoretic objects?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A poset (P, ≤) is called continuous if it carries the standard order-theoretic notions of way-below relation ≪ and approximation, and bicontinuous if both (P, ≤) and its order-dual are continuous. A globally hyperbolic poset is a bicontinuous poset whose interval topology (generated by sets of the form ↑a ∩ ↓b) is locally compact and Hausdorff. The interval domain IP of such a poset is the set of nonempty closed order-intervals [a,b] = {x : a ≤ x ≤ b}, ordered by reverse inclusion, equipped with the Scott topology; this construction yields a category-theoretic equivalence between the category of globally hyperbolic posets (with suitable morphisms) and the category of interval domains.

A globally hyperbolic spacetime (M, g) — i.e. a time-oriented Lorentzian manifold admitting a Cauchy hypersurface — becomes such a poset under the causal order ≤ given by the chronological/causal future. On M one may consider, besides the manifold topology τM, several finer topologies: the Zeeman fine topology τZ, Göbel's generalization τG (extending Zeeman's construction to curved spacetimes), and the Hawking–King–McCarthy (path) topology τHKM. Each of these strictly refines τM and is known to be non-metrizable.

Problem. Let (M, g) be a globally hyperbolic spacetime, viewed as a globally hyperbolic poset, and let IM be its associated interval domain with the Scott topology.

(a) Provide a precise, mathematically rigorous procedure that reconstructs a topology on M from purely order- and domain-theoretic data of IM, and characterize which topologies on M (manifold, Zeeman, Göbel, Hawking–King–McCarthy, or others) can be recovered in this way.

(b) Determine whether the non-metrizability of the topologies τZ, τG, τHKM — together with the order-theoretic and topological structure of the interval domain IM — singles out a canonical "spacetime topology" on M distinct from the manifold topology τM that is intrinsic to the interval-domain model.
artifact.status_search_result: Martin and Panangaden established that globally hyperbolic spacetimes form a category equivalent to interval domains and that the manifold topology can be recovered as the interval topology of the causal poset. However, no published work appears to address the rigorous reconstruction of non-manifold spacetime topologies (Zeeman, Göbel, Hawking–King–McCarthy) from interval-domain data, nor whether their non-metrizability picks out a canonical alternative spacetime topology. The question therefore appears to remain open.
